statement: I want the leases and nothing else: the biggest ones first, until the budget is spent. Oil has always paid for this company and I do not see why we should learn a new business now.

answers.context_and_stakes: If the leases are wrong the loss is the redevelopment capital spent now under an assumed cost grid; the worst case I have in mind is five years of $42 oil.
answers.parties: The committee wants the budget on what already produces; the lender wants a thin tail; the operator wants workovers it knows how to run; the grid operator decides nothing on the lease side, which is part of why I like it.
answers.emotional_investment: The company has run offshore oil for thirty years and I have defended the Gulf position in every budget round; the queue deposits already paid are small and I do not count them.
answers.evidence: I leaned on the flat-path lease NPVs and on every lease being positive at base; I passed over the scenario median, the high-cost case and the contracted wind requests that are positive.
answers.framing: I did not put a mixed book on the table, nor a smaller lease book that leaves room for the contracted wind requests.
